assets.description: Patient records containing medical history and test results
Patient records system used by doctors and nurses to consult and update files
Confirmation emails sent to patients after booking
Remote server access credentials and connection held by the external IT provider

vulnerabilities.description: Username and password authentication provides no multi-factor protection, making credentials susceptible to brute-force or theft.
Patient records may lack field-level access controls, allowing any authenticated user to view or modify all patient data regardless of role.
The public appointment website is exposed to the internet and may contain exploitable vulnerabilities such as SQL injection or cross-site scripting.
Confirmation emails may transmit patient appointment details in plaintext, exposing sensitive information in transit.
The external IT provider's remote access to servers is a privileged entry point that may not be subject to the clinic's security monitoring or access controls.

threats.description: An external attacker steals or guesses staff credentials to log into the patient records system and access confidential medical data.
A malicious insider such as a rogue doctor or nurse deliberately accesses or alters patient records beyond their authorised scope.
An external attacker exploits a vulnerability in the public booking website to gain unauthorised access to backend systems or disrupt the service.
An external attacker intercepts unencrypted confirmation emails to obtain patient appointment details and personally identifiable information.
A compromised or malicious external IT provider abuses its remote server access to exfiltrate patient records or sabotage the patient records system.
An external attacker compromises the IT provider's systems and uses the provider's remote access credentials to reach the clinic's servers.
A careless member of staff accidentally overwrites or deletes critical patient records during a routine update.
